name: Do I need a permit to remove a kitchen wall in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit to remove a wall for an open-concept kitchen conversion in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Do I need a permit to remove a wall for an open-concept kitchen conversion in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, wall removal for an open-concept kitchen conversion generally requires permitting in Los Angeles. If the project changes structural walls, openings, plumbing, electrical, or the kitchen layout, it is not treated like a simple cabinet swap or finish upgrade. The city typically wants plan review for the existing layout and proposed layout, and structural work may require engineered drawings. This is one of the biggest reasons open-concept projects fail to stay on schedule: homeowners assume demolition can start first, but the permit and engineering path must usually come before the work. If the home is in Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or another nearby city, the exact process can differ, but the same principle applies: once you alter walls or systems, approval is usually required. Before hiring, ask the contractor whether they handle permit drawings, structural coordination, and inspections, not just demolition.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. In Los Angeles, wall removal and changes to openings typically require a permit and plan check, especially when the work affects structure, plumbing, electrical, or the kitchen layout. Pure cabinet or finish updates may qualify for simpler permitting, but opening walls does not.
